scenes.title: Choose the directory and its categories
scenes.narration: Contacts gives your department a shared directory of people, organizations, and locations. Keep member accounts and roster roles in Personnel; use this directory for useful operational references. In our fictional Chicago Fire training department, we are in Contacts, on the Categories page. The category table separates its name, description, color, and contact count. It starts empty here, even though the department already has uncategorized contacts. We will create a small partner directory and verify each saved entry.

scenes.title: Create and verify a useful category
scenes.narration: Choose Add Category. Enter Academy Partner Directory as the Name and describe it as fictional training partners and logistics contacts. Keep the blue color so the category is easy to recognize. Display On Map remains unchecked and Map Icon stays Default. Those controls are separate from organizing the directory. Save, then read the returned category row. Its name, description, and blue color are present, while Contacts In Category is zero. That saved row is our starting point for adding contacts.

scenes.title: Prepare a person and a clear description
required_label_union: TRAINING ONLY - Fictional community partner liaison. Verify current contact details before operational use.
scenes.narration: On the Add Contact form, select Person, then Academy Partner Directory. Enter Sylvie and Brett in the first and last name fields. The organization field can add context; here it contains Academy Community Partners, marked fictional. Email Address and Cell Phone hold deliberately reserved training values. Scroll to Description and explain the purpose of the entry. Our text identifies a fictional community partner liaison and asks the reader to verify current details before operational use. Keep that description useful and specific.

To verify category membership, use the named category in the list or the edit form; the Additional Info category value on this View is numeric.

scenes.title: Add a separate organization
required_label_union: TRAINING ONLY - Fictional supply and mutual-aid coordination contact.
scenes.narration: Create a second entry using Location or Company. Keep the same category, leave the person name fields empty, and enter Academy Logistics Desk, marked fictional, in Company Location Name. The organization has its own reserved training email and an Office Phone ending in zero one four three. Its Description explains that it is a fictional supply and mutual-aid coordination contact. Using the appropriate contact type and phone field makes the directory easier to understand when someone else opens the entry.

scenes.title: Enter an explicit reference point and address
scenes.narration: In Location Info, GPS Location has a latitude field and a longitude field. Enter the complete fictional Chicago pair together. Entrance GPS Location and Exit GPS Location are separate pairs and stay blank in this exercise. Continue to Physical Address and enter the fictional Training Avenue street, Chicago, Illinois, and postal code. Check Same as Physical under Mailing Address, then use Save at the bottom of the form. These are stored directory reference values; entering coordinates does not establish a device position, a verified entrance, or a successful route.

scenes.title: Combine the category and text filters
scenes.narration: Back in Contacts, select Academy Partner Directory in the category tree. Both newly saved entries appear: the person and the logistics organization. Now enter Logistics in Search. The table narrows the selected category to the organization, and the count says that one result is filtered from two entries. Read the name and type before choosing View or Edit. A short list can reflect the combination of these filters, so check the selected category and search text before deciding that an entry is missing.

scenes.title: Verify location and copied address on the owning forms
required_label_union: TRAINING ONLY - Fictional supply and mutual-aid coordination contact.
scenes.narration: Open the saved organization. Contact Details shows its name and email, and Location Info shows the stored coordinate pair. Farther down, verify the physical address and original Description. For the named category and copied mailing address, return to the list and choose Edit. The category is selected by name, and the reopened mailing fields contain the copied street, city, state, and postal code. Same as Physical is clear on reopening here. Check those actual fields rather than assuming the blank mailing section on View proves that nothing was saved.

scenes.title: Verify a small saved change
required_label_union: TRAINING ONLY - Fictional supply and mutual-aid coordination contact.
scenes.narration: Use a small, easy-to-check edit to confirm your maintenance workflow. In the reopened organization form, Office Phone ends in zero one four three. Change that final digit to four. After saving and reopening the same contact, the field now ends in zero one four four. Read the reopened value, not just the value you typed. The original supply and mutual-aid Description remains in place. A successful change to one field is a reason to verify that field specifically, rather than assume every attempted edit was stored.

scenes.title: Review the finished directory and adapt it
scenes.narration: Finish in Categories. Academy Partner Directory now contains two contacts. Give someone responsibility for reviewing those details as partners change. Chicago Fire can use this pattern for logistics contacts. Community care and mental health teams can maintain operational partner directories without patient detail. Search and rescue can organize staging and support contacts; security teams can group site contacts; wildland crews can maintain supply references; and industrial response teams can organize facility coordination contacts. In each setting, choose clear categories, verify saved values, and keep the directory current.
